note: Mwalimu's first-time tips, one per interface beat (case ui.beats). Each fires once, on its trigger, in the first case that lists the beat. They teach how to use a tool, never what a case means. Triggers: caseOpen, sceneOpen, notebookOpen, boardOpen, chargeOpen, evidenceOpen (optionally limited to renders), afterWrong. Case 1's guided loop lives in case-001.json tutorial[]; the hint offer (case 7) is built into the charge sheet.

foundPaperBook.line: Registers are kept by people who weren't thinking about murder. That's why they're honest. Read every row, not just the one you came for.

timeWindow.line: Times matter now. Your notebook has a Time tab: everyone you can place, lined up on one clock.

map.line: Two places today. Both are in the folder. Go back and forth as often as you like. Walking costs you nothing.

paperMatch.line: When two papers talk about the same thing, put them side by side. Pin a line from each in your notebook and read the Pinned tab.

sceneSketch.line: A building, not a street. Before you decide who was where, ask how anyone got from one floor to another.

timeView.line: Open the Time tab. Every bar is someone you can place. The empty stretches deserve as much attention as the bars.

zoomInspect.line: Small writing matters. Tap any photograph to open it full size, then pinch or double-tap to look closer.

firstRedHerring.line: Not everything that looks guilty is. When something points at a person, ask what else could explain it before you write a name.

timetable.line: A timetable says where a train should be. People tell you where they were. Hold one against the other.

absencePreview.line: Read every exhibit twice: once for what it shows, and once for what it ought to show.

threeStepProof.line: This one takes three steps, not two. If your name rests on a single fact, you're not finished.

pinnedFacts.line: You can pin six facts. Keep the ones that belong together on the Pinned tab, and the board will show them too.

photoZoom.line: Photographs have backgrounds. Open it full size and look past the people in front.

twoBlankGroup.line: Two blanks this time, judged together. Halima accepts both or neither, so be sure of each.

credibilityStamps.line: See the five stamps on the folder? That's your credibility. Paperwork costs a stamp, and so does accusing someone with the wrong fact. Spend them like they're your own money.

pressClaim.line: From now on people lie to you. When something they say can't be true next to something you know, press it, and put that fact in front of them. Be sure first. A wrong guess costs a stamp.

guardedStance.line: Some people won't talk to you at all. Don't beg. Come back when you're holding something about them they can't ignore.

searchWarrant.line: That's a private place. You'll need a search warrant, and a magistrate needs grounds: something you already know that points there. It costs a stamp.

brokenIsntGuilty.line: A grey stamp. They lied, but the lie explains something innocent. A broken story isn't a confession, Amani. Keep going.

linkedClaims.line: One lie can hold up another. When it falls, the claims leaning on it fall too. Look at what else just got crossed out.

recordsRequest.line: Phone and mobile-money records need a court order. When you have grounds, the form appears on the folder. One stamp each. They don't lie, but they only answer the question you ask.

whyBlank.line: There's a second line on the sheet now: why. Halima won't take a killer without a reason a court will believe. Prove the motive like you prove the rest.

patternFileBlank.line: This sheet wants a pin from the Pattern File. Something you found in an earlier case belongs in this one. Halima wants the connection proven, not felt.

autopsyReport.line: An autopsy says what the body can prove. Read the findings, and read what isn't there. No head injury is a fact too.

labQueue.line: The lab works in hours. Send a test the moment you have what it needs, then keep working. Waiting with nothing else to do is the last resort.

arrestClock.line: You can detain a suspect now. Twenty-four hours, then a court or the door. Detain when you can use the time: samples first, the lab next, the questions that need results last.

howGroup.line: New line on the sheet: how. Not the weapon you'd guess. The one the evidence proves.

whenWindow.line: A new line on the sheet: when. Not a guess at the hour. The window the evidence closes from both ends: the last time they were seen alive, and the first time they were not.

whenFromBothSides.line: Close the window from both sides. One fact says no earlier than this, another says no later than that. The answer is what is left between them.

timelineRail.line: Along the bottom of the board: every time you have found, in order. It is not graded. It is where a story that doesn't fit the clock starts to show.

timelineStrip.line: This one wants the night in order. Put each event in its time. Some times are there to tempt you, and stay empty. It all has to be right for Halima to accept it.

siteMap.line: The Mara is big. Your sites are on the map with the drive between them, and every drive moves the clock on. Plan your route. Don't drive back across the reserve for one question.

whereBlank.line: New line on the sheet: where. Not where she was found. Where she died. A body can be moved. Mud, blood and a radio log stay where they were.

whereCulprit.line: This where isn't the scene. It's where he really was when his alibi says he was somewhere else. Find the fact that puts him there, at that minute.

twoBlankWhere.line: Two places on this sheet: where he was killed, and where the lease files went. Both come from the same list. Prove each one on its own.

documentTools.line: From here on, paper can lie. When a document matters, put it beside one you trust and compare them: numbers, stamps, signatures, dates. Whatever does not match is your tell.

forgeryGroup.line: New line on the sheet: which document was forged, and what shows it. Name the paper, and the one flaw a court can see. A guess about who wrote it is not a tell.

lawyeredSuspect.line: An advocate. Your questions will get you nothing now. Find the fact that changes the case against the client, and put it in front of the advocate. Guess, and you lose a stamp.

twoValidTells.line: This forgery has more than one flaw. Any tell you can prove will do. Pick the one you understand best.

expectedList.line: Up here, look for what isn't there. Every place has things that should be: a dog that barks, a fire that was lit. When you know why one should be there, check it. Missing is a fact too.

absenceGroup.line: New line on the sheet: what was missing, and what that proves. Pick the absence, then say what it shows. An absence only proves what it rules out.

refutedAbsence.line: An absence proves less than it seems. Before you build on one, ask what else could explain it. If something else could, it doesn't prove your point.

secondSentence.line: A second sentence on the sheet: who helped, and how. If nobody did, say nobody. Someone who helped without knowing is not an accomplice.

suspectedPlanted.line: Some of what you found was put there for you to find. Name the planted item, and the flaw that shows it was planted. Evidence that is too convenient deserves a second look.

realTarget.line: The one who died is not always the one who was meant to. Ask who the poison, the trap, the bullet was meant for.

twoGrips.line: Two names this time. Two people did this together. Either order, but both must be proven.

reviewerSwap.line: Halima can't review this one. Rukia Hassan will. She doesn't know you, and she won't make allowances. Make it airtight.

wholeDesk.line: Everything you have filed in a hundred cases is on this desk. The Pattern File has six threads. Each one ends at the same door.

signsAsEvidence.line: Read the walls as well as the people. A painted sign, the hours on a door, a notice on a board: they are facts too, and they don't lie.

portraitAsEvidence.line: A face can be evidence. Open a portrait full size and look at what they wear and carry, not just who they are.

languageAsEvidence.line: Tap any underlined word for its meaning. And remember Swahili time: the hours count from six in the morning, so saa moja is seven o'clock.

readingStatement.line: Read a statement line by line: who was paid, when, and what failed. A reversal or a failed payment says as much as one that went through.

twoLiars.line: More than one person can lie in the same case, and one lie can cover another. Break one, then go back to the others with what it gave you.

sortTheLiars.line: Look at the mark when a claim breaks. Red means it points at them. Grey means it only embarrasses them. Two liars, two different reasons.

deadZone.line: No signal is a fact too. A phone that couldn't reach any mast tells you something about the place it was in.

honestMistake.line: Not everyone who's wrong is lying. An honest mistake gets an amber mark, not red or grey. Mistaken people have nothing to hide; they just saw it wrong.

countingAsEvidence.line: When there's a count, do the sum yourself: what there should be, what was used, what's left. The difference is a fact.

expertWitness.line: Some witnesses know things no lab does. An old hand's knowledge is evidence like any paper; read it as carefully.

devicesRemember.line: Machines remember times. Anything with a time on it goes on the board's timeline rail, next to what people told you.

natureAsClock.line: The sky keeps time too. Moon, tide and dark are on the rail like any clock.

playlistAsClock.line: Anything that runs in order is a clock: songs, buses, shifts. Put it on the rail and look for the gap.

machineDiary.line: A machine's log is a statement nobody can coach. Lay it on the rail beside the people's.

machinesThatCount.line: Meters count hours and kilometres whether anyone wants them to or not. Do the arithmetic.

waterAsMap.line: Water moves things. On this map, notice which way the river runs.

coverageMaps.line: A radio or a phone only reaches so far. On the map, the shaded ground is where it could be heard.

readWholeDocument.line: Read the whole document: the headings, the columns, the small print at the foot. Not just the line that caught your eye.

magnifierOnStamps.line: From now on, use the Magnifier. Drag it over every stamp and signature and look at the ink itself, then compare it with paper you trust.

signatureOverlay.line: Try Overlay. It lays one sheet over the other like tracing paper. Slide it until the parts that should match sit on top of each other.

indexMapOverlay.line: Overlay works on plans too. Lay one drawing over the other and line up the edges.

twoWillOverlay.line: Lay the two papers over each other. Real signatures never match perfectly; a perfect match is a tracing.

overlayRecords.line: Records can be overlaid like paper. Lay one over the other and see whether the lines move together.

textComparison.line: Words can be compared like signatures. Lay one text over the other and read where they differ.

routinesAsEvidence.line: A routine is a clock. When someone's day always runs the same way, the moment it stopped is a time.

allysTranslations.line: A translation is someone else's words. If a statement came through an interpreter, ask yourself what might have been left out.

trackersReading.line: Ground holds marks for hours. Read the tracks the way a tracker would: which way, how heavy, walking or dragged.

sweptYard.line: A swept yard shows every step taken since. Look at what the broom lines say about who walked where.

theSeat.line: Things are set for the last person who used them: a seat, a mirror, a shelf. Ask who that would fit.

theRack.line: Check every slot against the book that lists it. An empty slot with an entry against it is a fact.

gapRuler.line: Numbered logs should run without gaps. Read down the numbers; a missing one is something that was taken out.

core.notebookOpen: Everything you find lands here by itself. People, places, exhibits, and times. You don't write, you think.
core.boardOpen: The board is yours. Drag things where they make sense to you, tie string between them. Nobody grades it.
core.phoneOpen: Call me when you're stuck. Where to look, what to notice, or the answer. Each one costs you a star you haven't earned yet, never the case.
core.chargeOpen: The charge sheet. Only names you've actually found are in the bank. Halima reads every one.

hintOffer: Detective. You can call me. "Where to look" names the thing that matters. "What to notice" shows you two facts that belong together. "The answer" fills a blank, and costs you more.
